oss.description: Debloat any Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and get an Apple TV-style home.
oss.readme:
**The viral tweet:** [x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102)

On 17 October 2026 I posted a before and after of my parents' TV, cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi.
It reached 7.4M views, people started doing the same to their own TVs, and their replies turned into
the lists here: 170+ TV models from 200+ contributors in four days. The repo was called tv-vibehack
until the 19th; old links work.

## How it works

Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's
developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling:

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Back up** | The list of installed packages and settings. |
| **Disable** | The manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk, with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. |
| **Install** | A small native launcher, made the default home screen. |

**No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.**

The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask
before touching anything you might use.

## Quick start

You need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access.

Any of these work: Claude Code (on [0G Private Computer](https://pc.0g.ai) or an [Anthropic plan](https://claude.com/pricing)), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) or [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli).

| Where | What to do |
|---|---|
| **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. |
| **2. On your computer** | Paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) into your assistant and fill in your TV model. |
| **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, which four go in the dock, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. |

The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with
screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes.

## What you get

A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way:

| Part | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| **A pitch-black home** | A dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. |
| **A top shelf** | Names the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. |
| **The rest of your apps in a grid** | Slides up when you press Down. |
| **One floating glass highlight** | Springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. |
| **Three frosted buttons** | Inputs (HDMI ports under the names you gave them in the TV's settings, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. |
| **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** | In [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit), and a matching Clock screensaver. Set `show_stats` in config or a theme for one line under the clock: CPU, free memory and free storage. It stays off unless you turn it on, and it refreshes only while Home is on screen. |
| **Themes and module cards** | Themes change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and module cards let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. |

And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics
phoning home, no apps you never asked for.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![The top shelf names the focused app over an ambient glow in its colour](docs/focus-2-up-netflix.png) | ![The Inputs popup: HDMI ports with what is connected, AV and Live TV](docs/inputs-menu.jpg) |
| *Top shelf and ambient glow* | *Inputs: HDMI with connection state, AV, Live TV* |
| ![The grid with the glass highlight on a tile and its name beneath](docs/focus-1-fancode.png) | ![The Clock screensaver: a thin clock drifting over the glow](docs/clock-screensaver.png) |
| *The grid, one glass highlight, the tile's name* | *Clock screensaver, drifts so nothing burns in* |
| ![The aurora theme: a wallpaper and tinted pills, pushed without a rebuild](docs/theme-aurora.jpg) | ![Six columns and a six-app dock from a theme's config.json](docs/theme-six-columns.jpg) |
| *Aurora theme, pushed with `tools/theme.sh`* | *Six columns and a six-app dock, same launcher* |

## Supported TVs

Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**.

| Platform | What works |
|---|---|
| **Android TV, Google TV** | The debloat and the launcher. |
| **Fire TV** | The debloat half only, since Fire OS will not hand Home to a third-party launcher. And on the 2015 Fire TV Box (Fire OS 5) even that half fails: every `pm` route is refused. |
| **A few China-market TCL sets** | They refuse to install any launcher at all; their lists say so in the header. |
| **Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS)** | Different systems. See [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md) for a webOS port, and [docs/devices/samsung-tizen.md](docs/devices/samsung-tizen.md) for what a 2021 Samsung set answers over Wi-Fi (no ADB, so no `pm disable-user`) if you are weighing a Tizen port. |

  扫码或搜索群号加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。

---

## 亮点

- **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。
- **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。
- **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。
- **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。
- **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。
- **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。
- **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。
- **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。
- **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。
- **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。
- **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。
- **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。
- **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。

oss.readme:
# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

Feature details and configuration

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

### Build from source

Before building DeepInfer, please create and activate an empty Python 3.12 environment.

``` bash
# Use `ascend` instead for the Ascend platform
# Keep it exported in the environment where you run DeepInfer
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh
```

### Offline inference

The default checkpoint, [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), is
downloaded into the Hugging Face cache on the first run; set `DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` to
run from a local copy instead.

``` bash
python examples/offline_inference.py
```

See [examples](examples/README.md) for details.

## Performance benchmarks

| Prefill | Decode |
| :---: | :---: |
| [![Prefill: non-cached input throughput vs. latency](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png)](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png) | [![Decode: output throughput vs. per-user speed](doc/images/decode_pareto.png)](doc/images/decode_pareto.png) |

Measured on 4 SM100 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode — each within one scale-up domain. To reproduce the benchmarks, see [run_sweep.sh](examples/sweep/run_sweep.sh).

## Evaluation benchmarks

See [eval/README.md](eval/README.md).

## License

DeepInfer is released under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgments

DeepInfer was originally built primarily on [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), with additional inspiration from [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM). We thank their developers.

## Citation

```bibtex
@misc{deepinfer2026,
  title = {DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models},
  author = {DeepSeek-AI},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer}},
}
```

Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

  
  
  
  

  
    
  

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent:
prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the
process of optimizing that system.

Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an
open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It
connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed:

* **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task
  through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe
  their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral
  contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback.
* **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness*
  with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide
  future refinement.

  
    
  

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a
single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base
harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on
JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the
task-level recursion budget brings further gains.

The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and
Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**.

## Video overview

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f-9aa5-a93662df4d56

## Contents

- [Video overview](#video-overview)
- [Harness components](#harness-components)
- [Install](#install)
- [Run a benchmark](#run-a-benchmark)
- [Experiments](#experiments)
- [Web access](#web-access)
- [Results and resume](#results-and-resume)
- [Citation](#citation)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)
- [Disclaimer](#disclaimer)

## Harness components

Harness² exposes eight editable components around the model: **system prompt,
guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, and plugins**.
They control context construction, the tool interface, delegation, and behavior
inside the tool loop.

  
    
  

## Install

Use **Linux, Python 3.12, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)**.
From the repository root:

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e '.[render]'
harness2-demo --output runs/demo --k 2
```

The local demo runs both recursion modes with deterministic editors and real
Python executions. It requires no model credentials.

For model-backed benchmarks, install **Node.js 20+, the Google Cloud CLI**, and
the [benchmark dependencies](docs/SETUP.md#requirements). LAB needs Pandoc and
Poppler; WorkBuddy-Bench needs Docker. Then configure your models:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your Vertex AI project and model IDs.
gcloud auth application-default login
```

See the [setup guide](docs/SETUP.md) for model settings, authentication
alternatives, and the [Codex executor](docs/SETUP.md#codex-executor).

## Run a benchmark

The following example installs LAB and runs one task, then evaluates and reports
its result. Model-backed runs incur API costs; start with a small task selection.

```bash
harness2-setup lab
harness2-check --bench lab
harness2 --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel \
  --only-domains antitrust-competition --max-tasks 1
harness2-judge --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel
harness2-report --bench lab --k 1 --mode parallel
```

Sequential recursion runs the same commands with `--mode sequential`. `--k` is
the task-level recursion budget; see [Experiments](#experiments). Judging and
reporting must use the same benchmark, executor, subset, `--k`, `--mode`, and
seed as the refinement run. Add `--dry-run` to `harness2` to preview task
selection without model calls.

| Benchmark | Tasks | Install | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| JobBench | Professional work | `harness2-setup jb` | [JobBench](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#jobbench) |
| LAB | Legal work | `harness2-setup lab` | [LAB](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#lab) |
| WorkBuddy-Bench | Office, web, and code | `harness2-setup wb` | [WorkBuddy](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#workbuddy-bench) |

Choose one benchmark per command. WorkBuddy also takes `--subset office`,
`--subset web`, or `--subset code` on every command after setup. The
[benchmark guides](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) cover each one's data, domains, and
grading.

## Experiments

Scale task-level recursion in two ways: **parallel recursion** explores multiple
candidate harnesses and composes refinements from their execution evidence;
**sequential recursion** carries the refined harness and accumulated evidence
through successive Propose–Probe–Compose steps.

  
    
  

Parallel recursion explores wider; sequential recursion refines deeper.

| Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--k 1` | One Propose–Probe–Compose step |
| `--k K --mode parallel` | Probe `K` general and `K` domain-specific candidates, then produce `K` compositions |
| `--k K --mode sequential` | Refine the harness through `K` successive steps |
| `--substrate cx` | Use Codex instead of the default OpenCode executor |

After each task, harnessing-level recursion retains the adopted harness and
evidence-supported lessons to guide future refinement. See the
[experiment guide](docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) for task selection, concurrency,
reproducibility, and baseline comparisons.

## Web access

Executor network access is unrestricted, and Codex runs with its sandbox
disabled. Public benchmark rubrics may be accessible online. Before evaluation,
configure [network restrictions](docs/EXPERIMENTS.md#web-access) to prevent
access to benchmark answers and grading criteria.

## Results and resume

Results are saved under `runs/`, organized by benchmark and subset where
applicable. They include task summaries, deliverables, adopted harnesses,
reflection notes, and evaluation results.

    Stays on your computerNothing is uploaded. Filee works offline and saves the result next to the original.
  

## See it in action

  
  Watch the 27-second video and try the interactive demo on filee.sh

## Install

Download from [Releases](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee/releases/latest).

- **Windows 10/11**: run `Filee--win-Setup.exe`, or unzip the `win-Portable.zip` and run `Filee.exe`.
  Setup is Filee's own installer, in Filee's languages, and needs nothing else on the PC. It can add the Explorer
  menu, start at sign-in, the `filee` command and optional engines; silent installs take Inno Setup's switches
  (`/VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES`).
- **macOS 13+** (preview): unpack the `osx-arm64` or `osx-x64` package and run `./install.sh`.
  The build isn't notarized yet, so allow the first start in System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**.
- **Linux x64/ARM64** (Ubuntu 22.04+): unpack the package and run `./install.sh` (no root, needs Python 3).
  Drag gestures need X11. On Wayland, use the drop zone and the file manager's right-click menu.

Filee shows new releases in its menu and updates itself, keeping your settings and engines. After an update, a few
slides show what's new.

## Features

- **A donut at the cursor**: hold a key, drag files and drop them on a format. Only formats that fit the files appear.
- **Straight from the browser**: drag a picture, a link to a file or a download out of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari the same
  way. Filee saves it to your Downloads folder (or keeps only the converted file) and converts it. Links are downloaded
  without your browser's sign-in.
- **One toolbar per file type**, arranged by drag and drop, with presets for quality, size, DPI, PDF pages and compression,
  video and audio, output folder and file names.
- **Two sides to every donut**: press Tab or turn the mouse wheel while it is open to flip it over to less common formats and tools.
- **Crop before converting**: the Crop slice opens pictures one by one. Drag the frame, pick a ratio, and only that part is saved.
- **Many files at once**, in parallel. Routes with several steps (HWP → HWPX → DOCX) are found automatically.
- **Watch folders** convert every file that lands in them.
- **Recent conversions** on Home, each with a thumbnail: open the result, or open it with another app.
- **Other ways in**: the right-click menu, a keyboard shortcut, the drop zone and the [`filee` command](#command-line).
- Light and dark themes with your own accent colour and donut opacity, in English, Español, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文, Polski, हिन्दी, Русский, العربية (right to left) and Português (Brasil).

oss.readme:
PhotoCraft

  Image editing; an open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop, rebuilt in pure Rust.
  Layers, masks, adjustment layers, layer styles, type, vectors, brushes and real PSD files,
  in a native app written entirely in Rust. Open source, offline, and yours.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  

  

  PhotoCraft on getartcraft.com ·
  ArtCraft ·
  All Crafting Apps

  
  
  A caption card with a drop shadow, live type, and Vibrance and Curves adjustment layers, with the Curves editor open.
  The Great Wave off Kanagawa, Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1831

> [!NOTE]
> **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Digital, generative, music,
> games — if you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

  Features ·
  Everything in the box ·
  PSD ·
  Agents ·
  Under the hood ·
  Get started ·
  Downloads ·
  Crafting Apps ·
  Discord

  
    
      🎛️ Familiar by design
      The menus, shortcuts, panels and tools are where your hands expect them, from ⌘J to ⇧⌘D. If you know Photoshop, you already know PhotoCraft.
    
    
      ⚡ Native and fast
      A GPU compositor on wgpu (Metal, Vulkan, DX12, WebGPU), copy-on-write tiles and multithreaded filters. No Electron, no web view, no waiting.
    
    
      🗂️ Real PSD files
      Open, edit and save layered Photoshop documents. Re-saving keeps the render of 307 of the 309 psd-tools test files.
    
    
      🤖 Agent-ready
      Every action is a command, so you can drive the same engine from the UI, the CLI, a JSON control channel or an MCP server.
    
  

## Features

Every screenshot here is the real app at work on public-domain art, rendered offscreen through its control channel.

  
    
      
      
      Levels and Vibrance adjustment layers, with the live Histogram panel.Impression, Sunrise, Claude Monet, 1872
      Edit without regret
      Adjustment layers keep every edit live. Stack Levels, Curves, Vibrance, Hue/Saturation and a dozen more, mask them to an area, reorder them, or turn them off, and your original pixels never change.
      
      16 adjustment layers that also apply directly to pixels, including Curves with per-channel editing, Levels with a live histogram, Black & White, Channel Mixer, Gradient Map, Photo Filter, Selective Color and Color Lookup (.cube, .3dl, .look). Plus Shadows/Highlights, Replace Color, Match Color, HDR Toning, Desaturate and Equalize.
    
    
      
      
      Outer Glow and Stroke on a live type layer, in the Layer Style dialog.Earthrise, William Anders / NASA, 1968
      Styles that sell the shot
      Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Outer and Inner Glow, Bevel & Emboss, Satin, Stroke, and Color, Gradient and Pattern Overlay, live on any layer, including type. Patterns come from a library (built-ins, Edit › Define Pattern, .pat import/export) and PSD Patt blocks.
      
      Copy and paste styles between layers, hide all effects at once, and open styles straight from your PSDs, rendered to match Photoshop.
    
  
  
    
      
      
      An elliptical selection becomes the mask of a Hue/Saturation layer, so only the face keeps its color.Girl with a Pearl Earring, Johannes Vermeer, c. 1665
      Selections that understand your image
      Marquees, lassos and the Magic Wand for precision; Quick Selection, Object Selection and Select Subject when you want the computer to do the tracing; Select and Mask to refine hair-fine edges.
      
      Feather, expand, contract, smooth, grow, reselect. Turn any selection into a layer mask, a vector path or a shape. Smart selection runs on your machine, with no cloud and no account.
    
    
      
      
      A headline edited in place, with a byline and a paragraph of body text.Among the Sierra Nevada, California, Albert Bierstadt, 1868
      Type that sets beautifully
      Point and paragraph text, edited right on the canvas, with full Character and Paragraph controls: font, weight, size, leading, tracking, alignment and colour. The full Type Color Picker also supports screen sampling with a pixel loupe.
      
      Type layers stay editable, take layer styles, and round-trip through PSD.
    
  
  
    
      
      
      A badge made of shape layers: a gradient-filled lotus, a star and a dotted ring.Water Lilies, Claude Monet, 1906
      Pixel-perfect vectors
      Rectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Polygon, Line and the Pen, Freeform Pen and Curvature Pen tools, with resolution-independent shape layers, gradient fills, and dashed, aligned strokes.
      
      Combine shapes (unite, subtract, intersect, exclude), keep paths in the Paths panel, use them as vector masks, or stroke and fill them. 116 of 116 shape layers in our PSD corpus match Photoshop's pixels.
    
    
      
      
      Twirl previews live on the canvas, only inside the selection.The Starry Night, Vincent van Gogh, 1889
      See it before you commit
      Every filter dialog previews live on the canvas, through your selection. Blurs (Gaussian, Box, Motion, Radial, Surface, Smart, Lens, Shape, and the Blur Gallery: Tilt-Shift, Iris, Field, Spin, Path), sharpening, Reduce Noise, distortions (Twirl, Wave, Ripple, Displace, Shear, Zig Zag…), Pixelate, Stylize (Oil Paint, Wind, Extrude…), Render (Clouds, Fibers, Lens Flare, Lighting Effects) and more.
      
      Run filters on a smart object and they stay editable: change, hide, reorder or mask them at any time.
      
      Large-radius blurs use running-sum box passes across all cores: a radius-180 Gaussian on 3.6 MP takes under a second.

releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- [#15611](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15611) [`4508172`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/45081725e9e5cb79b76ade277a7e61395cb55950) Thanks [@taylorlee](https://github.com/taylorlee)! - Allow `wrangler dev` to start module Workers without a default export

  Previously, `wrangler dev` failed to start module Workers that exported only named entrypoints, such as RPC services, unless an unused default export was added. These Workers now start normally in local development without that workaround.

- [#16370](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16370) [`61fc739`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/61fc7397b2982db1c9b099cbeaee3fd0428fdf8a) Thanks [@WalshyDev](https://github.com/WalshyDev)! - Fetch the remote config diff from the configured compliance region

  When a Worker was last deployed from the dashboard, `wrangler deploy` and `wrangler versions upload` download its remote configuration to compare with the local one. These requests ignored the `compliance_region` field in the Wrangler configuration file and only honoured the `CLOUDFLARE_COMPLIANCE_REGION` environment variable. A FedRAMP High Worker configured through the config file would send them to `api.cloudflare.com` instead of `api.fed.cloudflare.com`, and the deploy would fail with authentication errors. They now use the same compliance region as the rest of the deploy.

- [#15846](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15846) [`a88cac4`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/a88cac4d880629a4ad68f7173b3353941bea6081) Thanks [@oddharsh](https://github.com/oddharsh)! - Fail with an error instead of hanging when local dev requests can't work under Bun

  Bun's `fetch()` ignores the undici `dispatcher` that Miniflare routes requests through (oven-sh/bun#39247). Under Bun, `createTestHarness()`'s `server.fetch()` and `server.getWorker()`'s `fetch()`, `email()` and `scheduled()` now throw a `UserError`, requests to the dev server URL get a 503 naming the cause, and starting remote bindings throws a `UserError`. Each of these used to hang with no error. `server.getWorker().getEnv()` and `getExport()` keep working under Bun.

- [#16359](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16359) [`262021d`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/262021dd0db4d24df33405d89e4c1a6622ce832f) Thanks [@tw4](https://github.com/tw4)! - Stop `--strict` deploys and version uploads from aborting when the API omits optional binding fields
